name: Sonoma Mountain

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sémillon, Cabernet Franc and Tempranillo fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Pinot Noir is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

soil.rock: Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 2°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.
